definition: A patch lies closer to A when it shows more ridges, branching hollows, dark slope shadows and coarse, irregular land-cover patches, with fewer broad, smooth agricultural parcels. B is dominated by open green fields with clear boundaries and relatively little visible relief.
cues: Ridges and shadowed hollows in A versus comparatively smooth terrain in B.
Irregular, coarse-textured cover in A versus broad, clearly bounded field mosaics in B.
Mostly muted or dark near-infrared reds in A versus extensive bright red fields in B.
Roads and clearings winding around terrain in A versus field-aligned lanes and hedgerows in B.
